title: Does It Fit: CPU, Memory and Flash Budgets for a Small Board, the Peak a Short Test Never Sees, and What Heat Takes Away

questions.question: A planner measured for 60 s on the bench shows a peak of 0.40 cores. In the field its peak is 2.00. What went wrong?
options: The planner has a bug that only shows in the field
The test was too short to see the replan that comes once in 70 s
The board in the field is slower
The bench measured cores and the field measured percent
questions.explanation: The largest sample is a lower bound on the real peak. The replan that takes 2.0 cores comes once in 70 s, and a 60 s test contained none. The average hardly changed: 0.40 against 0.42.

questions.question: Why is there an allowance of 70 percent on the CPU average and 80 percent on memory, and not 100?
options: At 100 percent a CPU misses deadlines when anything coincides, memory kills a program, and flash cannot write the next update
Half is kept back for a second copy of each program
The allowances are a convention with no reason behind them
Because the measurements are 30 percent too low
questions.explanation: A system at its limit does not slow gracefully. The allowances are the room that keeps coincidences from becoming missed deadlines and killed programs.

questions.question: The board throttles to 60 percent in a hot box. What happened to the same six programs?
options: Nothing: throttling only affects peaks
They fit better, since they run cooler
Memory went over, since slow programs hold more
Over on both CPU average (2.60 against 1.68) and peaks (4.90 against 3.00)
questions.explanation: They fit cool and not hot. At 60 percent the four cores are worth 2.4. The same programs that fit a cool board are over on both the average and the peaks.

questions.question: A map server of 1500 MB is added and it is idle. What is over?
options: CPU average, since one more program runs
Flash, since the map is large
Everything: one program too many
Memory only: 3530 MB against 3277 allowed, since its CPU is small
questions.explanation: The server is idle, so it adds little CPU. Its 1500 MB takes memory past the 80 percent allowed, and memory has no slow failure.

questions.question: What does keeping two slots do to the release that fits?
options: Nothing: slots share their space
It doubles it, since there are two places to put it
It halves it: 6273 MB with two against 12546 MB with one, for 16 GB of flash with 2 GB of data and 200 MB of logs
It removes the limit
questions.explanation: The room left after data and logs is divided between the slots. Two slots are what make the safe install of 20-05 possible, and they cost half the space.

questions.question: Why is a fit on paper not a fit?
options: The arithmetic of the check is approximate
The peak is only as good as the longest run measured, and the board, its box and its temperature are real
A fit on paper is a fit, if the allowances are met
Paper cannot record peaks
questions.explanation: Run the whole robot on the real board, hot, for a shift. The profile only knows the peaks that happened while it was being measured, and the throttling depends on the real box. The check is a screen.
